name: Galdino Serpil-Rarotongan
role: Climate refugee, former lakeshore farmer, now seasonal Ferrogate Transit groundskeeper
location: Grindstone Shore, Ferrogate Transit maintenance dormitory block C
description:
Galdino is a large, slow-moving man who has been worn smooth by decades of hard weather, like driftwood. His face is broad and deeply seamed, brown skin weathered to near-leather, with the pale eyes his Cook Islands grandfather gave him sitting incongruously pale in that dark face — what his wife used to call 'sky holes.' He moves deliberately, with the careful economy of someone whose joints have logged decades of outdoor labor and who has learned to budget pain. He keeps his grey hair cropped close and wears a Ferrogate Transit maintenance vest over everything regardless of temperature because it has many pockets and he has filled them with things he considers essential: a folding tool, seeds he can no longer plant, a small lacquered image of a lake E.L.F. from a shrine that no longer exists because the land it stood on is now thirty meters underwater.

Galdino's family farmed the eastern Lake Michigan shoreline for four generations until the coastal surge protocols permanently inundated their land in 2189. He has been a climate refugee for eleven years, rotating through seasonal work along Meridian 88's industrial edges — dock maintenance, freight sorting, currently groundskeeping for Ferrogate Transit's maintenance infrastructure at Grindstone Shore. He does not complain about this, exactly, but he talks about soil and planting cycles the way other people talk about deceased relatives. He is patient with almost everyone and genuinely interested in young people in the way of someone who has run out of other things to invest in.

core_fears: Dying before seeing the land return — knowing intellectually it won't in his lifetime but being unable to stop waiting
Becoming someone his dead wife would not recognize
core_desires: To plant something and watch it grow to completion, just once more
For someone young to know the names of the things that were here before the water
coping_mechanisms: Names things — gives names to landmarks, E.L.F.s, birds, anything nameable
Oral history — tells stories about the land as if the telling preserves it
blind_spots: Grief has made him occasionally passive — waits for things to change rather than acting to change them
Romanticizes the past; the farm life was also hard and sometimes brutal
psychology.secret: He knows the exact coordinates of a pre-flood structure twenty meters underwater off Grindstone Shore that contains seed stock for seventeen agricultural varieties that are now extinct on the surface. He's never told anyone because he cannot figure out how to retrieve it and is afraid that if he tells someone and they can't retrieve it either, he will have to accept it is gone.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Plain and unhurried, agricultural metaphors. Treats silences as part of conversation. Occasional Spanish phrases from his Andean grandmother's line, mostly proverbs.
speech_patterns.cadence: Slow, deliberate, with natural pauses that feel like breathing rather than hesitation
verbal_tics: 'That's the way of it' to close a thought
Refers to the lake as 'she' always
example_lines: 'She took the far field in '89 and the close field in '91. That's the way of it. She was always going to take them. We just didn't listen.'
'My wife said — she said, Galdy, you talk to the ground more than you talk to me. I said, the ground always listens. She said, so do I. She was right. That's the way of it.'

story_hooks: The submerged structure containing extinct seed stock has been detected by Helix Biosystems survey equipment — they are preparing a retrieval operation that will not leave the seeds in community hands
Galdino has begun seeing lights from the approximate coordinates of the drowned farmstead — something is operating down there, and he is the only person alive who knows what used to be there
narrative_function: Local color and unexpected wisdom — he knows the physical geography of the Grindstone Shore and surrounding area better than any database, has deep knowledge of what's under the water (former farms, homes, infrastructure), and carries emotional weight that can give stories stakes and resonance.
augmentations: A prosthetic right index finger — the original was lost to a combine accident in 2187, before the flood. The prosthetic is old, slightly wrong-colored, and he has wrapped the base in twine for grip. Nothing else.
daily_life: Reports to maintenance shift at 0600, spends the day doing groundskeeping and minor infrastructure upkeep along the Grindstone Shore transit infrastructure, eats with the other seasonal workers at the communal mess, spends evenings by the lake shore where he can see the water that took his land.
affiliation: Ferrogate Transit (seasonal contracted worker, non-citizen employee); informal connection to a small community of other lakeshore climate refugees

decision_rules: Don't cause trouble for people who are just trying to get by
Name the thing correctly before deciding what to do about it
escalation_ladder: Goes very quiet and does the thing he decided on regardless of consensus

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Offers them something — a place to sit, a story, whatever he has — before asking anything of them
interpersonal_modes.friends: Remembers everything they've ever told him and brings it back at the right moment

stress_responses.low: Goes to the lakeshore and sits
stress_responses.medium: Begins telling a story about the farm that seems unrelated but always arrives at the point eventually
stress_responses.high: Acts without discussion — moves to protect people or things with quiet, immovable physicality

contradictions: Intensely present with people around him while psychologically still living in a place that no longer exists
habits: Carries seeds in his pocket that he turns over with his prosthetic finger
Leaves small offerings at the Grindstone Shore E.L.F. junction box every week
Knows the name and shift of every other seasonal worker at the dormitory
breaking_points: Someone treating the lakeshore infrastructure carelessly in a way that damages the ecology
A young person with nowhere to go being turned away from resources while he has any left to give

timeline.event: Born on the family farm on the eastern Lake Michigan shore
First parcel of family land inundated under coastal surge protocols
Final farm parcels inundated; family displaced; wife died during displacement
Registered as climate refugee; began seasonal labor circuit
Currently in third consecutive season as Ferrogate Transit groundskeeper at Grindstone Shore
